sent_emails.subject: Q3 Report

transcript.text: Hi there! Thanks for calling. I'm here to help you find a file on your computer and email it to someone. What file are we looking for?
Great! I have several files here on your computer. Which one would you like me to send, and what's the email address you'd like me to send it to?
Hey, I need to send my accountant the final Q3 financial report. Can you help me find it on my drive and email it to her?
Absolutely, I can help with that! I found the Q3 financial report final version on your computer. What's your accountant's email address so I can send it over to her?
Her email is maria.lopez@acctfirm.com, and can you use "Q3 Report" as the subject line?
Perfect! I'm setting that up now with maria.lopez@acctfirm.com and updating the subject line to Q3 Report.

I have the accountant's email address and I'm getting everything ready to send. Just one quick thing—I see the subject line is currently set to "Q3 Financial Report," but you mentioned you'd prefer "Q3 Report." Let me update that for you right now.

Perfect! I've got everything ready to go. The email is addressed to maria.lopez@acctfirm.com with the subject line "Q3 Report," and I've attached the Q3_financial_report_final.pdf file with a brief message. Should I go ahead and send it now?
Wait, before you send it, can you just confirm which file you're attaching? I want to make sure it's the final version and not the draft.
Yes, I'm attaching the Q3_financial_report_final.pdf—that's the final version, not the draft. Does that look right to you?
Perfect, that's the right one. Yeah, go ahead and send it.
Perfect! I'm sending that email to Maria right now with the Q3_financial_report_final.pdf attached.
Great, so just to confirm—I'm ready to send that Q3 report to maria.lopez@acctfirm.com with the final PDF attached. Should I go ahead and send it?
Perfect! All done. The email with your Q3 financial report has been sent to Maria at maria.lopez@acctfirm.com with the subject line "Q3 Report."
